# Brag Plan: Vinea

## What is this app?

Vinea is a modular autonomous harvesting robot for Dutch commercial greenhouses — a Fairino FR5 on a pipe-rail trolley that finds tomatoes with a camera, plans a route that clears the crop it is *not* picking, and harvests them. It is built entirely in MuJoCo simulation, deliberately, with no hardware budget yet. The impressive part is not that it works; it is that the project measured itself as **22.7× short of its own design target** and put that number at the top of its own README.

## The angle

Every robotics launch video is a victory lap. This one opens with the failure metric.

The repo's own words: the 22.7× shortfall "is the most useful thing in this repo. It was found in a simulator in August, before a cent was spent on an arm, which is the entire argument for building it this way." That is the brag — not the robot, the *discipline*. A solo, pre-funding, pre-hardware project that would rather publish a bad number early than a good number late.

So the video is a deadpan engineering post-mortem that happens to be beautiful. Real simulation footage, real logged numbers, no adjectives. The machine looks completely convincing while the captions calmly explain that it does not exist. The humour is entirely the project's own — it comes from the gap between how finished the footage looks and how unsparing the text is.

This is specific to Vinea and could not be reused: the numbers, the shortfall, the "on purpose", and the footage are all this repo's.

## Hook (first 2-3 seconds)

A wide, darkened shot down a greenhouse aisle — the trolley travelling the pipe rail, rows of tomatoes either side. No logo, no product name, no setup.

Then one line, slammed in and held:

> **22.7× short.**

A brag video that opens by telling you the number is bad. That earns the next twenty seconds.

## Key moments (the middle)

- **The money shot.** One unbroken take of the whole cycle at close range: the gripper cradles a six-tomato truss, the stem is cut, the cluster is carried back across the aisle, and it drops into the crate on the machine's own deck. Over it, the wordmark and the deadpan reveal that no hardware has been built.
- **The robot's own eye.** The wrist camera feed with the HSV ripeness classifier's decisions burned in — live `RIPE` boxes on the fruit it will take, none on the fruit it won't, and the running `N FOUND / N RIPE` readout at the bottom. This is the product *deciding*, not a diagram of deciding. Over it, the three logged numbers arrive one by one: **57** logged picks, **46%** clean, **0** collateral damage.
- **The point.** The Week 4 free-placement scene — fruit put anywhere, the route re-planned mid-run — under the line that is the whole argument: *found in a simulator, before a cent was spent on an arm.*

## Outro / punchline

The wordmark, and then the honest roadmap item stated as a to-do list entry:

> **Next: make it 22.7× better.**

The joke is that it is not a joke — closing that gap is literally the sprint's outstanding deliverable.

## User flow worth showing

The product is a robot, so the "user flow" is the pick cycle, and all three beats exist as real recorded footage:

1. **Entry / perceive** — the wrist camera finds fruit and classifies ripeness on its own (`wrist-eye`, `use_truth=False`: nothing in that run was told where a tomato is).
2. **Key action** — approach, cradle the truss, cut the stem (`pick-crate`).
3. **Result** — carry across the aisle and release into the crate (`pick-crate`, same unbroken take).

The centerpiece scenes (2 and 3) show exactly this. No landing-page recreation is used anywhere — the project's real renders are stronger than anything that could be rebuilt in HTML.

## Tone

- Preset: **deadpan**
- Creative direction: *an engineering post-mortem that happens to be beautiful*
- Interpretation: long holds, few words, big empty space, and absolutely no hype adjectives. The footage carries the polish; the type stays flat and factual and lets the numbers be the shock. Every claim on screen is quoted or derived from the repo's own README. Pace comes from cutting on the music's beats, never from pulling text away before it can be read.

## Format: landscape — 1920x1080
## Duration: 22.4 seconds

## Visual identity (from the project)

Taken verbatim from `tools/record.py`'s `Lens` class, which defines the palette the project's own site and video overlays use:

- Background / ink: `#0F1512` (green-black)
- Text / chalk: `#EDE8DD`
- Accent / signal: `#E2724F` — commented in the source as *"ripe. The page's reserved colour."* Used only for the ripe/accent beat, never decoratively.
- Muted / secondary: `#8A8377` (commented *"unripe"*)
- Display font: a clean grotesque (Inter) — the project has no web font in-repo; this matches its plain, technical register
- Body / figures font: a monospace (JetBrains Mono) for every measured number, because the whole video is about measurements
- Strongest visual element: the recorded simulation footage in `capture/raw/` — five clean 1920x1080 single-camera takes with no instrument panels burned in. The `wrist-eye` clip already carries the project's palette in its overlay.
- Colour grade: reuse the project's own house grade from `tools/publish.py` (`eq=saturation=0.78:contrast=0.96` + warm `colorbalance`), and its hero lift-and-cap darkening for the two text-heavy scenes, so the video matches the site's published clips exactly.

## Share copy (draft)

Built an autonomous greenhouse harvester in simulation, measured it honestly, and it came out 22.7× short of target. Publishing that number is the whole point — it cost a laptop instead of a robot arm.

## Audio direction

- Role: **sparse bed that builds once** — quiet and almost empty under the hook, arriving properly for the numbers, and never triumphant.
- Music: `happy-beats-business-moves-vol-12-by-ende-dot-app.mp3` (bundled). Chosen specifically because its first 8 seconds are genuinely sparse (beat intensities dip to 0.10/0.12/0.13) and the first strong cue does not land until 8.74s. That gives a restrained, deadpan opening that arrives exactly where the evidence does.
- Music treatment: start at 0:00, low bed throughout (roughly -18 dB posture), no swell on the hook, and a clean fade under the final wordmark so the last line reads in near-silence.
- Audio-reactive treatment: **none**. Deadpan tone; the footage is already doing the work and pulsing anything would break the register.
- SFX posture: **sparse**. At most three or four cues in the whole video. One soft hit for the hook line, one restrained cue per stat arrival, nothing on the outro.
- Audio-coupled moments: the three stat figures in Scene 3 arrive one by one on strong cues; the hook line lands on the first beat.
- Restraint rule: no risers, no whooshes on every transition, no impact stingers on the outro, nothing celebratory. If a cue would read as "hype", leave it out.

## Music cue guidance

Track: `happy-beats-business-moves-vol-12-by-ende-dot-app.mp3`, tempo **109.96 BPM**, preset read from the bundled cue file.

- **Primary lock — 8.74s**: the first strong cue in the track (intensity 0.985) and the end of the sparse intro. Cut into Scene 3 (the evidence) here. This is the single most important sync point.
- **Secondary lock — 15.84s** (intensity 0.960): the payoff line *"Before a cent was spent on an arm."* lands here.
- **Third lock — 18.56s** (intensity 0.992): cut to the outro.
- Beat-grid window for the sequential stat reveal: strong cues at **8.74 / 10.93 / 12.55**. Deliberately spaced ~1.6–2.2s apart rather than on consecutive beats, so each figure clears the readable floor. Do not tighten these to every beat.
- Restraint note: deadpan tone — use these three or four locks and ignore the rest of the grid. The track has dense strong beats from 8.74s to 15.84s and snapping more reveals onto them would make the video feel like an ad.

## Source footage (already recorded, in-repo)

`capture/raw/*.mp4` — 1920x1080, 60 fps, clean single-camera renders produced by `tools/record.py`. In/out points below were chosen from contact sheets and cross-checked against the author's own published edit points in `tools/publish.py`.

| Scene | Clip | In → Out | What is on screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `whole-house.mp4` | 2.00 → 6.39 | Aisle-level establishing shot, trolley on the pipe rail |
| 2 | `pick-crate.mp4` | 31.00 → 35.35 | Gripper cradles the truss, cut, carry, release into the crate |

| 5 | `row-load.mp4` | 4.00 → 7.81 | Wide row shot, stems detaching under load |

## Storyboard

### Scene 1 — The number — 4.39s (0.00 → 4.39)

`whole-house` footage, darkened with the project's own hero lift-and-cap grade so type sits cleanly over it. Slow, almost still. Nothing moves fast.

**22.7× short.** slams in at 0.56s in chalk `#EDE8DD` at display scale, and holds for the rest of the scene. At 1.64s a muted second line fades under it: *"of the throughput it was designed to hit."* Both stay on screen until the cut.

No logo yet. The viewer does not know what this is, and that is the hook.

Sequential/interaction: yes — two lines, the big figure first at 0.56s, the qualifier at 1.64s, both holding to 4.39s (2.75s+ settled each).
Audio intent: near-empty. The track's sparse intro, low. The line should feel like it landed in a quiet room.
Audio-coupled idea: one soft, dry hit on the 0.56s beat as the figure lands. Nothing else.
Music: sparse intro, low bed.
Transition mood: clean → Scene 2

### Scene 2 — What it is, and what it isn't — 4.35s (4.39 → 8.74)

`pick-crate` footage at the house grade, full frame, undarkened — the truss cradled, cut, carried and dropped into the crate. This is the most convincing four seconds the project has.

Lower-third block: **VINEA** in chalk at 4.90s, then *"An autonomous tomato harvester."* muted at 5.45s. Then at 6.60s, in signal `#E2724F`: **No hardware. On purpose.**

The accent colour is spent here and nowhere else in the video, which is how the project's own site uses it.

Copy source: compressed from the README's verbatim *"No hardware budget yet, on purpose"*.

Sequential/interaction: yes — three text beats at 4.90 / 5.45 / 6.60, all holding to the cut (accent line settled 2.14s).
Audio intent: the bed continues building underneath. Still restrained. The viewer should be watching the robot, not listening.
Audio-coupled idea: none — let the footage play clean.
Music: building, still low.
Transition mood: hard cut on the 8.74s strong cue → Scene 3

### Scene 3 — The evidence — 5.46s (8.74 → 14.20)

Cut lands on the track's first strong cue. `wrist-eye` footage at the house grade — the robot's own camera, with its live `RIPE` boxes and `HSV COLOUR THRESHOLD · N FOUND · N RIPE` readout already burned in from the original render.

A small muted monospace eyebrow at 8.74s: `MEASURED IN SIMULATION · 4 CROP DENSITIES`.

Then three figures arrive one at a time, each a large monospace number with a small muted label under it:

- **57** — logged picks — at 8.74s
- **46%** — clean — at 10.93s
- **0** — collateral damage — at 12.55s

All three hold together until the cut. The `0` is the one that should feel like the flex, and it gets the longest silence after it.

Copy source: README Week 4 campaign — "57 logged attempts across four crop densities", "clean picks 26/57 — 46%", "collateral damage 0".

Sequential/interaction: yes — three stat blocks revealed one by one on strong cues 8.74 / 10.93 / 12.55, spaced 1.6–2.2s apart so each clears the readable floor; the last holds 1.65s settled.
Audio intent: the track has arrived. This is as energetic as the video gets, and it is still restrained.
Audio-coupled idea: one short, dry, non-celebratory cue per figure — a click or a soft card-place, not an impact stinger. Three cues total, same sound each time.
Music: full bed, low in the mix.
Transition mood: clean → Scene 4

### Scene 4 — The point — 4.36s (14.20 → 18.56)

`replan` footage at the house grade — the plain Week 4 test rig, which reads visually as a simulator rather than a greenhouse, and that is exactly why it is here. The arm carries a fruit whose position it was never given.

At 14.20s, a muted line: *"The shortfall was found in a simulator."*
At 15.84s, on the secondary strong cue, the payoff in chalk at display scale: **Before a cent was spent on an arm.**

This is the thesis of the entire project and it is the README's own sentence.

Sequential/interaction: yes — setup line at 14.20s (4.36s settled), payoff line cue-locked at 15.84s (2.72s settled).
Audio intent: hold steady. Do not swell. The line is not triumphant and the music must not make it sound triumphant.
Audio-coupled idea: none. The payoff line lands on the music's own cue; that is enough.
Music: steady bed, beginning to thin.
Transition mood: clean → Scene 5

### Scene 5 — Outro — 3.81s (18.56 → 22.37)

Cut on the 18.56s strong cue. `row-load` footage, darkened back down to the hero grade so it recedes behind the type.

**VINEA** in chalk at 18.56s. At 19.66s, in signal `#E2724F`: **Next: make it 22.7× better.** At 21.28s, small and muted: `getvinea.nl`.

The last line is the punchline and it is completely sincere — a validated kg/hr is the sprint's outstanding deliverable.

Sequential/interaction: yes — three beats at 18.56 / 19.66 / 21.28, holding 3.81 / 2.71 / 1.09s.
Audio intent: the bed fades out under the wordmark so the final line reads in near-silence.
Audio-coupled idea: none. No outro stinger — a hit here would undo the whole register.
Music: fading to nothing by 22.37s.
Transition mood: fade to ink.

# Hyperframes Composition Brief: Vinea

## Objective

Create a short launch-style brag video for Vinea — a simulation-first autonomous greenhouse harvesting robot — whose whole angle is that it opens with its own bad number.

## Output

- Composition directory: `brag-output/composition/`
- Rendered video: `brag-output/brag.mp4`
- Format: landscape — 1920x1080
- Duration: 22.4 seconds

## Source Material

- Project root: `/home/krishaanth/Desktop/personal_projects/github/vinea`
- Primary files read: `README.md`, `tools/record.py` (palette + clip subjects), `tools/publish.py` (the author's own edit points and colour grades), `capture/raw/*.mp4`
- Product name: **Vinea**
- Tagline / strongest claim: *"The design target is 24,000 kg/week/robot. This is 22.7× short. That is the most useful thing in this repo."*
- Key UI or visual moment to recreate: **nothing needs recreating.** The project ships five clean 1920x1080/60 single-camera renders of the real simulation. They are already cut, graded and placed in `assets/video/`. The `wrist-eye` clip carries the project's own ripeness-classifier overlay in the project's own palette — that is the product visibly making a decision, and it is stronger than any HTML mock.

### Copy that must appear verbatim

- `22.7× short.`
- `No hardware. On purpose.` *(compressed from the README's "No hardware budget yet, on purpose")*
- `57` / `logged picks`
- `46%` / `clean`
- `0` / `collateral damage`
- `Before a cent was spent on an arm.`
- `Next: make it 22.7× better.`
- `getvinea.nl`

Every one of these is sourced in the claim audit at the bottom of `brag-plan.md`. **Do not add any claim that is not in that table.** This project's entire credibility is that it does not overstate, and a fabricated number in the video would undo the thing being bragged about.

## Creative Direction

- Tone preset: **deadpan**
- Creative direction: *an engineering post-mortem that happens to be beautiful*
- Interpretation: long holds, few words, generous empty space, flat factual type. The footage supplies all the polish; the typography must not perform. Pace comes from cutting on the music's cues, never from pulling text off before it is read. No hype adjectives anywhere.
- Angle: Every robotics launch video is a victory lap; this one opens with the failure metric. The repo measured itself 22.7× short of its own design target, in a simulator, before buying any hardware — and put that at the top of its README. The brag is the discipline, not the robot. The humour is the gap between how finished the footage looks and how unsparing the captions are.
- Hook: a darkened aisle-level shot of the trolley on its rail, then `22.7× short.` slammed in and held. No logo, no setup.
- Outro / punchline: `Next: make it 22.7× better.` — sincere, because a validated kg/hr is the sprint's outstanding deliverable.

### Avoid

- Generic SaaS language
- Abstract filler visuals — every frame is real recorded simulation footage
- Any celebratory or triumphant treatment; it contradicts the source material
- Redesigning or re-grading the footage — the grades are the project's own and are already baked in
- Any number not in the claim audit

## Visual Identity

Taken verbatim from the `Lens` class in `tools/record.py`, which defines the palette used by the project's site and its video overlays.

- Background / ink: `#0F1512`
- Text / chalk: `#EDE8DD`
- Accent / signal: `#E2724F` — source comment: *"ripe. The page's reserved colour."* **Spend it on exactly two lines in the whole video** (Scene 2's `No hardware. On purpose.` and Scene 5's `Next: make it 22.7× better.`) and nowhere else.
- Muted / secondary: `#8A8377` — source comment: *"unripe"*
- Display font: **Inter** (variable, shipped at `assets/fonts/inter-var.woff2`)
- Figures / labels font: **JetBrains Mono** (variable, shipped at `assets/fonts/jbmono-var.woff2`) — every measured number is mono, because the video is about measurements
- Visual references from the project: the house colour grade and the hero lift-and-cap darkening, both lifted from `tools/publish.py` and already applied to the clips in `assets/video/`

## Storyboard

Use the storyboard in `brag-output/brag-plan.md` as the creative contract.

Scene summary:

1. **The number** — 4.39s (0.00→4.39) — `22.7× short.` over a darkened greenhouse aisle. Must be read before anything else appears.
2. **What it is, and what it isn't** — 4.35s (4.39→8.74) — the full pick cycle; `VINEA`, then the deadpan reveal in accent.
3. **The evidence** — 5.46s (8.74→14.20) — the robot's own camera with its live ripeness overlay; three logged figures arrive one by one on strong cues.
4. **The point** — 4.36s (14.20→18.56) — the free-placement test rig; the README's own thesis sentence.
5. **Outro** — 3.81s (18.56→22.37) — wordmark, punchline, URL, fading to ink.

### Prepared media (do not re-cut)

`assets/video/` holds the five clips already trimmed to their scenes with ~0.3s of tail, and already carrying the project's own grades:

| File | Scene | Grade |
|---|---|---|
| `s1-house.mp4` | 1 | hero lift-and-cap (darkened for type) |
| `s2-pick.mp4` | 2 | house grade |
| `s3-wrist.mp4` | 3 | house grade |
| `s4-replan.mp4` | 4 | house grade |
| `s5-row.mp4` | 5 | hero lift-and-cap (darkened for type) |

## Audio

- Audio role: **sparse bed that arrives once** — near-empty under the hook, properly present for the evidence, never triumphant.
- Audio arc: silence-adjacent → single arrival at 8.74s → steady → fade to nothing under the final line.
- Music: `assets/music/happy-beats-business-moves-vol-12-by-ende-dot-app.mp3`
- Music treatment: start at 0:00, low bed throughout, no swell on the hook, clean fade-out across the outro so `Next: make it 22.7× better.` reads in near-silence. Deadpan tone — keep the bed well under the footage.
- Music cue guidance: bundled preset read from `assets/music/cues/…vol-12….music-cues.json` (tempo **109.96 BPM**). Locks, in priority order:
  - **8.74s** (intensity 0.985, first strong cue and the end of the sparse intro) — cut into Scene 3 here. Primary lock.
  - **15.84s** (0.960) — the payoff line lands here.
  - **18.56s** (0.992) — cut to the outro.
  - Sequential stat reveal grid: **8.74 / 10.93 / 12.55** — deliberately ~1.6–2.2s apart so each figure clears the readable floor. **Do not tighten to consecutive beats.**
- Audio-reactive treatment: **none**. The tone forbids it; pulsing or glow-breathing would break the register.
- Audio-coupled moments:
  - Scene 1, 0.56s — the hook figure lands — one soft dry hit, nothing more
  - Scene 3, 8.74 / 10.93 / 12.55 — the three figures — one short dry cue each, the *same* sound each time
  - Scene 5 — outro — **no cue at all**
- SFX selection guidance: sparse, four cues maximum in the whole video. Dry and short: interface clicks or soft card-places rather than impacts, risers or whooshes. Nothing that reads as celebratory. If a cue would make the video feel like an ad, leave it out.
- SFX analysis guidance: `/home/krishaanth/.claude/plugins/cache/brag/brag/0.2.2/skills/brag/assets/sfx/sfx-analysis.md` — prefer low high-frequency-risk sounds, especially for the three repeated stat cues.
- Exact SFX choice: Hyperframes chooses filenames, timestamps and volume once the animation exists.
- Audio files: copy the chosen music and any selected SFX into `brag-output/composition/assets/`.

## Hyperframes Instructions

Load the composition-building Hyperframes domain skills — `hyperframes-core`, `hyperframes-animation`, `hyperframes-creative`, `hyperframes-keyframes`, `hyperframes-cli`. This is the `/brag` workflow: do not enter the `hyperframes` entry-point intent interview and do not route into its generic promo / launch-video workflow. Prefer native Hyperframes conventions over anything in `/brag`.

Requirements:

- Show real product material — satisfied by the five recorded simulation clips; at least Scenes 2 and 3 must read clearly as the robot working.
- Keep all text readable: short labels ≥0.8s settled, sentences ≥0.3s/word. The timings in the storyboard already satisfy this — do not compress them.
- Keep the video within 15–25 seconds (target 22.4s).
- Include the music layer and a maximum of four dry SFX cues.
- Treat `/brag` audio notes as guidance; choose exact SFX after the visuals exist.
- Treat music cue metadata as timing hints. Use the three or four named locks and ignore the rest of the grid — the track has dense strong beats from 8.74s to 15.84s and snapping more reveals onto them would make this feel like an ad.
- Use local assets for audio, video and fonts. No network fetches at render time.
- Run `hyperframes check` before render — it is brag's single gate.

### Environment notes for this machine

The host has Node 20 and no system FFmpeg, both of which hyperframes refuses. A session-local Node 22 and a static ffmpeg/ffprobe are installed in the scratchpad and must be on `PATH` for every hyperframes invocation:

```bash
SP=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-krishaanth-Desktop-personal-projects-github-vinea/13541274-b8ab-4deb-8255-3b8b5be898ef/scratchpad
export PATH=$SP/node-v22.20.0-linux-x64/bin:$SP/bin:$PATH
```

Chrome is the system `/usr/bin/google-chrome`, so rendering falls back to screenshot capture rather than the `beginFrame` fast path. That is a speed characteristic, not a correctness one.

## Validate

```bash
cd brag-output/composition
npx hyperframes check   # brag's single pre-render gate — fix every error it reports
```

Fix all errors. `check` is brag's single pre-render gate — run it and fix everything it reports, including WCAG contrast failures (they gate as errors, not warnings). Each contrast finding carries a suggested compliant color, so apply it or adjust within the palette family and re-run `check` — most fixes need no screenshot. There is no per-element contrast escape hatch for real text; the only bypass is `check --no-contrast`, which skips the entire WCAG pass (all-or-nothing), not a way to accept one borderline element. For exact contrast thresholds, layout escape hatches, and reporting details, follow the current hyperframes-cli `check` guidance. `check`'s layout pass backstops the "keep all text readable" creative law — fix any reported overflow.

For a visual gut-check before rendering, optionally capture key frames:

```bash

```

## Preview

```bash
npx hyperframes preview
```

Tell the user the preview is running and give them the localhost URL. Invite them to check it before rendering.

If the user approves or asks to render:

## Render

```bash

```

This outputs to `brag-output/brag.mp4` (one level up from the composition directory).

For a faster iteration render:
```bash

```

For final delivery:
```bash

```

## Pick the poster frame

The poster is the still shown before the video plays — the first thing anyone sees when it's idle or unplayed. Don't leave it to the raw first frame or an arbitrary timestamp; those land on fades, mid-transitions, blank intro backgrounds, or half-rendered text.

You built this composition, so you already know its strongest moment and exactly when it lands — the hook line, the hero reveal, or the final logo. Pick that beat at a **settled** point: text fully animated in, before it exits (the storyboard timings tell you the safe window). Then extract that one frame full-res with ffmpeg. From `brag-output/composition`:

```bash
# use the timestamp of your strongest settled beat, e.g. 3.2s
ffmpeg -ss 3.2 -i ../brag.mp4 -frames:v 1 -q:v 2 ../brag.jpg
```

Aim for a frame that's postable on its own (the "show the thing" law — any frozen frame should be shareable). If the pulled frame lands on a transition or mid-animation, nudge the timestamp a few tenths of a second and re-extract.

### Bake the poster as frame 0

A bare `.mp4` has no `poster` attribute — every player and platform picks its own idle thumbnail, and almost all of them grab **frame 0**. Slack, Twitter/X, and Discord regenerate thumbnails server-side and ignore embedded cover-art metadata, so the *only* reliable way to control the idle image everywhere is to make frame 0 *be* the poster.

Replace **only** the first frame's pixels with `brag.jpg`, leaving every other frame and all timing untouched — same duration, same frame count, audio copied through. At 30fps the poster shows for 1/30s before the intro rolls, so it's imperceptible on playback but it's what every thumbnail grabber sees. From `brag-output`:

```bash
ffmpeg -y -i brag.mp4 -i brag.jpg \
  -filter_complex "[0:v][1:v]overlay=0:0:enable='eq(n,0)'[v]" \
  -map "[v]" -map 0:a? -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -preset slow -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  -c:a copy -movflags +faststart brag.poster.mp4 \
  && mv brag.poster.mp4 brag.mp4
```

The poster (`brag.jpg`) matches the video's dimensions because it was pulled from the same render, so the overlay lines up exactly. - Specific to the project — no generic "excited to share" language
